name: Chemical relaxers, often started in childhood
what_people_do: Use a lye or no-lye relaxer to straighten the hair every few weeks to months, often starting as a girl.
why_they_say_it_works: Straight hair is easier to manage and long seen as "professional"; family tradition.

documented_by.source: Hair product use and breast cancer risk among African American and White women, 2017, Carcinogenesis, PMID 28605409
documented_by.quote_or_summary: Breast cancer case-control study controls: relaxer use 88% of African American vs 5% of White women.

documented_by.source: Hairdressing and scalp disease in African adults (Cape Town, n=874), 2007, Br J Dermatol, PMID 17725667
documented_by.quote_or_summary: Cape Town adults: 49.2% of women had relaxed hair and 9.6% permed.

documented_by.source: Hairdressing and scalp disease in African schoolchildren (n=1042), 2007, Br J Dermatol, PMID 17553035
documented_by.quote_or_summary: Cape Town schoolchildren (1,042): 78.4% of girls had chemically relaxed hair.

documented_by.source: Hair dye and relaxer use among women in Embu and Nakuru, Kenya, 2024, PMID 39063423
documented_by.quote_or_summary: Embu and Nakuru, Kenya, 746 women: nearly 60% had ever used chemical relaxers.

documented_by.source: Hair grooming practices of women of African descent in London, 2016, J Eur Acad Dermatol Venereol, PMID 27038251
documented_by.quote_or_summary: London, 242 women of African descent: relaxers applied about every 88.6 days on average.

evidence.finding: Traction on relaxed hair carried 3.47 times the odds of traction alopecia vs natural hair.

source.name: Determinants of marginal traction alopecia in African girls and women, 2008, J Am Acad Dermatol, PMID 18694677

evidence.finding: Some hair products associated with breast cancer; relaxer links varied by group; authors call for further examination.

source.name: Hair product use and breast cancer risk among African American and White women, 2017, Carcinogenesis, PMID 28605409

harm_note: Associated with traction alopecia when combined with tight styling; a cancer association is reported but unsettled.
gaps: Fibroid and early-puberty links (PMID 22234483) seen as titles only.
